messages:
maria: quick update from today's attention kernel sampler runs — I ran a seqlen x batch sweep across A100, H100, and L40S for the new sampler policy (PR #4123). artifacts: https://ci.redwood/rep/4123/artifacts (perf traces + flamegraphs)

kevin: awesome, any glaring regressions?

maria: overall latency improved for short seqs (<=512) with fused-flash variant on all cards. BUT H100 shows a regression for seq=4096 when batch>=8 — latency jumps ~18% vs baseline fused-flash.

sahil: hmm, is that kv-cache related or kernel fallback?

maria: profiler shows increased memory stall time and a fallback to the tiled/spill path. stack snippet from perf-bot (flame):

```
gpu_driver -> cuBLAS -> fused_flash_attn_kernel
  -> kv_cache_load
  -> tiled_attention_spill_path
```

kevin: did the sampler policy choose paged-flash for those configs or forced fused?

maria: policy picked fused by score, but runtime decided to fallback when memory pressure + seq*batch*dim exceeded threshold. the decision point is in kernel_selector.cc: try_alloc_kv_cache().

ben: that sounds like our conservative kv spill threshold bitrotted after the batching heuristics change. we lowered the batch threshold last month, right?

maria: yep — change from #3980 reduced min_batch_to_use_paged from 12->8 which exposed new combos. on H100 the allocator fragmentation pattern is worse for 4k seqs.

perf-bot: uploaded detailed counters: A100 (run-1809876001).json, H100 (run-1809876002).json, L40S (run-1809876003).json

kevin: can you paste the key counters for H100 (seq4096, b=8)?

maria: sure — top-line numbers (H100, seq4096, b=8, model dim=4096):
- tokens/sec: baseline-fused 810 -> sampler-policy 664 (18% drop)
- GPU util: baseline 92% -> sampler 95% (more busy but stalled)
- DRAM reads: +27% (kv spill path)
- kernel_launch_count: +3 (extra tiled kernels)

sahil: that +DRAM reads suggests we hit a path that streams KV to host or slower device memory. any nvprof hints?

maria: nvprof shows two larger memcpy peaks right before the tiled kernel call. looks like a KV cache spill to device global mem and then re-load per micro-batch.

ben: action idea: revert the min_batch tweak for now and re-run the sampler scoring so we don't choose fused for these combos. also add a detection so kernel_selector avoids fused if estimated working set > device_local_safe_limit.

kevin: agree. also add a microbenchmark that reproduces seq4096 b>=8 on H100 with dim variants so CI can catch this. put a perf-unit test under perf/attention/sampler_h100_seq4096.sh.

maria: filing follow-ups:
- revert PR #3980 (rollback min_batch_to_use_paged) -> created issue https://go/repro/issue/577
- add runtime guard in kernel_selector (PR draft #4150)
- perf CI microbench (branch perf/sampler-h100-4096) -> will upload job

ci-bot: started nightly perf job perf/sampler-h100-4096 (job id 6654). logs: https://ci.redwood/job/6654

sahil: also worth checking tokenizer chunking artifacts — larger kv entries from certain bpe merges can increase cache pressure. did you use the same tokenization?

maria: yes identical tokenization. I also ran an opt run with quantized KV layout (qkv-16-pack) and that reduced DRAM reads but increased compute a bit — net win for A100/L40S, neutral on H100.

ben: for timeline: revert now, land selector guard next week, re-run full sweep on H100 and A100 after that. if CI microbench fails we'll pin the sampler policy for enterprise clusters until stable.

kevin: thanks — one more ask: can you attach the flame SVG and the tiny perf diff table to the issue? makes triage faster.

maria: done (attached). tagging @sre for H100 cluster flakiness check. :megaphone:

perf-bot: note: regression threshold exceeded for H100 seq4096 b=8 (18%). auto-created regression ticket reg-912 in tracking board.

ben: perfecto. wrapping up: small rollback + guard + microbench. sounds good to everyone? :+1:

kevin: +1

sahil: +1

maria: starting rollback now (PR #4160). will post run updates here.
